clue.text: Official statement to crowd about tenancy agreement

parts.note: to crowd is to press, as a throng presses round someone
re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
a lease is the contract under which a tenant rents property

explanation.surface: An announcement is made to a crowd regarding a rental contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A document issued to journalists giving an organisation's formal announcement.

clue.text: Banter concerning role, extremely emotive

parts.note: re is a short word meaning concerning or regarding
an actor's role is the part they play

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters of emotive, its first and last

explanation.surface: Teasing chatter about someone's acting role turns very emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick witty exchanges of remarks, a synonym for teasing banter.

clue.text: Demonstration succeeded — and how!

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees and lists of monarchs

explanation.surface: A display was a triumph, and what a triumph!
explanation.walkthrough: 'and how!' looks like an exclamation of praise, but HOW is simply taken as written after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A show is a display or exhibition, as when goods are put on show for a demonstration.

clue.text: Misleading clue embarrassed Holmes, initially slipping up

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of Holmes only

parts.note: erring means making a mistake, slipping up

explanation.surface: A false lead in a detective story leaves Sherlock Holmes red-faced as he blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion planted to lead investigators astray, the idiom from a strong-smelling fish once dragged across a trail.

clue.text: Slowly encircling a shed

indicators.note: encircling says the word for slowly wraps round the letter given by a

parts.note: lento is the musical direction meaning slowly

explanation.surface: Someone is gradually walking round a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple outbuilding propped against a wall, a kind of shed.

clue.text: Passionate — that could be us after a second run out

indicators.note: after places the word us behind the pieces that come before it

parts.note: mo is short for a moment, a second
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A team cries out after one of its batsmen is run out within a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that could be' is a link: it says the pieces that follow could make up the answer. 'after' puts US behind A, MO and RO; RO is the scorer's abbreviation for a batsman run out in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means full of romantic desire, a near synonym for passionate.

clue.text: English country gentlemen holding answer for realtors

indicators.note: holding says the run of English, country and gentlemen keeps the letter for answer inside it

parts.note: a state is a nation or country
gents is the informal word for gentlemen

explanation.surface: Rural English squires keep hold of a reply meant for property dealers.
explanation.definitionFit: Realtors is the American term for people who sell houses for clients, the same trade as the British name.

clue.text: Time for morning coffee in the Spanish square?

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
square as in all square means level, even

explanation.surface: Asking when the elevenses break comes round in a plaza in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a mid-morning snack or coffee is called elevenses, taken at around this hour; the question mark flags that the time is only typical.
explanation.definitionFit: The clock hour when the traditional British mid-morning coffee break is taken.

clue.text: Fielder's mistake

definitions.meaning: in cricket a ... is a fielder placed beside the wicketkeeper to catch edges
a ... is a small error, as in a ... of the tongue

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder drops a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for a close catching position in cricket and for a minor error.

clue.text: One excluded strange island abroad

parts.note: odd means strange
the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea, gives MAN
out can mean abroad, away from home, as in out there

explanation.surface: Someone is shut out of a peculiar island in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN comes from the Isle of Man, a self-governing island between Great Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The person left over or different from the rest of a group is the one who doesn't belong.

clue.text: Girl's coming across bound for a place down under

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name; the 's reads as is, the girl is doing something
to bound is to leap; she bounds, she springs

explanation.surface: A young woman leaps across to reach a spot in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl's coming across bound' reads as the girl leaping: ALICE then SPRINGS, a verb meaning bounds. 'coming across' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in the middle of Australia's Northern Territory; down under is slang for Australia.

clue.text: Irritable old servants

definitions.meaning: ..., like liverish, describes a bad-tempered mood once blamed on a sluggish liver
in old usage a household's servants in uniform were collectively called its ...

explanation.surface: Grumpy elderly domestic staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated adjective for tetchy, and the uniformed retinue of a great house in former times.

clue.text: Taste our fresh fish

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of taste our are made anew, rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner is invited to sample their freshly caught fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown trout that migrates to the sea, a game fish.

clue.text: Talk much about little sailor, a toad

parts.note: to natter is to chatter at length about something
jack is an informal name for a sailor, as in Jack Tar, a pet form of John

explanation.surface: Gossip at length about a young seaman, a toad of a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a toad' looks like an insult for the sailor, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small European toad with a yellow stripe down its back, known for its loud call.

clue.text: Lampstands precariously balanced by artist

indicators.note: precariously suggests the letters of balanced are unsteady and topple into a new order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: Light fittings are perched unsteadily by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link joining the rearranged CANDELAB to RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Candelabra are branched holders for candles or lights, a form of lampstand.

clue.text: Landmass — between seas, I assume

indicators.note: between says the letters sit across the words seas, I assume

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a continent lies between oceans.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent, a vast landmass.

clue.text: A dearth? Gather so, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that the letters of gather so turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone infers a lack of something with mild astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is a lack or scarcity, the same as a dearth.

clue.text: Band from the south has reformed

indicators.note: reformed says the letters of has are put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A musical group from the south has got back together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests a pop group re-forming; it is a strip of cloth. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist, a band.

clue.text: Country girl seen weaving ahead

indicators.note: ahead puts the rearranged letters in front of the word for girl
weaving suggests the letters of seen are interlaced into a new order

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A rural girl is spotted making her way forward through a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country girl' reads as one phrase, a rural lass, but 'Country' alone is the definition; 'weaving' is the anagram signal and 'ahead' fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Monument — one layer within gets treated

indicators.note: within says one and the word for layer sit inside the rearranged letters
treated suggests the letters of gets are processed into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
a hen is a layer, a bird that lays eggs

explanation.surface: A monument gets restored after one of its stone layers is processed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' is not a stratum of stone but an egg-layer; 'treated' signals the anagram (STGE) and 'within' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric circle of standing stones on Salisbury Plain in England, a famous monument.

clue.text: Drink in a mug

definitions.meaning: a small measure of drink, especially spirits
mug is slang for the face or head

explanation.surface: Having a drink served in a beer mug.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tot of liquor, and a slang word for the head, as mug is.

clue.text: Got the shakes in run-down part of city

indicators.note: shakes suggests the letters of got the are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Someone became nervous in a seedy area of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got the shakes' reads as a fit of nerves; 'shakes' rearranges GOT THE, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A deprived, densely crowded urban area, often one where a minority is segregated.

clue.text: Mexican with stock managed company employing that woman

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it, so managed gives ran

indicators.note: employing says the company abbreviation takes on the word for that woman inside it

parts.note: her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: A Mexican businessman ran a firm that hired a particular woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranchero is a rancher in Mexico or the US southwest, one who keeps cattle.

clue.text: Fear brawl must involve leader of rabble

indicators.note: must involve says the word for brawl takes in the next piece

parts.note: a brawl is a fight

indicators.note: leader of asks for the first letter of rabble

explanation.surface: Fear that a street fight will draw in the ringleader of a mob.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden shock of alarm, a synonym for fear.

clue.text: Lake in Maine, centre for crew

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

indicators.note: centre for asks for the middle letters of crew

explanation.surface: A lake in the state of Maine serves as a base for a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a small lake or pond, a word common in English place names.

clue.text: Gone out with one cutting art gallery deal

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of gone are knocked out of their order
cutting says the word for one slices into the art gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the famous art gallery in London
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dealer has left, and someone is slashing a painting at the gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' sits at the end looking like a noun for the gallery sale, but it is the verb; 'out' signals the anagram, 'cutting' the insertion, and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To negotiate is to bargain or settle terms, to deal.

clue.text: Keen, prima donna? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary signals turning the word for prima donna the other way round

parts.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer, a prima donna

explanation.surface: Is the leading soprano keen? Quite the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic, the same as keen.

clue.text: Publican in car next to curator

parts.note: a saloon is a car with a closed body and separate boot, a sedan
a keeper is a curator of a museum collection

explanation.surface: A pub landlord sits in a car beside a museum curator.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is the British name for a sedan car; 'next to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican runs a bar, and the person who runs a bar or saloon is its proprietor.
